title: The Dangers of Excessive Care for a Brother
english: Having drenched the sides [with tears], let us entreat God so that the night of the war may be dissolved and the light of the soul may be illuminated. Because of the service of a brother companion going abroad, according to the custom of prayers, renew the memory of this one; but do not imagine this beyond measure, lest the demons, having taken the beginning of care from you, sharpen this and extend it further, shadowing this for you in the singing of the psalms, and falling short in God of the care according to God, so that, striking back care with care, they may lead us captive from the superior ones, so that one does not consider the command: ‘Cast your care upon the Lord’ (Psalm 55:22). For they show, as if from the excessive care for the brother, that they also command griefs, subordinating the ruling faculty. Furthermore, they even reproach [you for] slowness, as if the brother had neglected the speed of the service, so that the much-caring longing might perhaps even turn into hatred. And it is a custom in the cares concerning the one away to do this also to the demons, in which they see him coming on the day, to mirror this one as a master, so that, as if from a dream that has passed, they may make us in the time of the ones away the prophets of dreams and again receive them, whom it is rather necessary to turn away and violently divert, lest from these they also lead the soul astray into other things.

Chapter 31. For these things indeed predict nothing, but they resent the things they see happening, and they imagine; indeed, often while we are being quiet, seeing a brother coming toward us, they mark us through thoughts, in which it is not right to believe, even if they think they are saying the truth; for through a certain truth they introduce a lie, so that they might map out the pitfalls on the paths in front of us by parts. Just as idle gold, being cast into a furnace, becomes purer, so also a soft monk, being refined in communal life, is made bright by his endurance; for he works to learn obedience through the command of the brothers; and through the striking [of trials], he prepares to have a nature of incense. When therefore he has endured insults with joy, and embraces lowliness with simplicity, having become superior to the things suffering against him, he strives to shine with virtues beyond, [with] the grace to him...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
